population.span: we recruited patients aged 18 years or older with community-acquired pneumonia from seven tertiary care hospitals in Switzerland within 24 h of presentation

endpoint.span: The prednisone group had a higher incidence of in-hospital hyperglycaemia needing insulin treatment

estimate.span: The prednisone group had a higher incidence of in-hospital hyperglycaemia needing insulin treatment (76 [19%] vs 43 [11%]; OR 1·96, 95% CI 1·31-2·93, p=0·0010).

treatment_strategy.span: Patients were randomly assigned (1:1 ratio) to receive either prednisone 50 mg daily for 7 days or placebo.

absent_reason.analysis_set: No source states the analysis set for the hyperglycaemia estimate. The only analysis-set statement ('analysed by intention to treat') is attached to the primary endpoint (time to clinical stability), so it is not bound here.

served_mismatch: Scale only: the served number (1.96, 1.31-2.93) equals the source value, but it is an odds ratio (source prints 'OR 1·96') while served_outcome.estimand and served_estimand are RR. Pooling it as an RR would be a scale mismatch; an RR would have to be recomputed from 76/392 vs 43/393 (the arm sizes come from the randomisation sentence, not from the estimate span). Endpoint is specifically in-hospital hyperglycaemia NEEDING INSULIN treatment, not any hyperglycaemia.

entry_population_matches_question.why: Adults (>=18 y) admitted to hospital with community-acquired pneumonia, randomised to prednisone added to care versus placebo.
entry_population_matches_question.span: we recruited patients aged 18 years or older with community-acquired pneumonia from seven tertiary care hospitals in Switzerland within 24 h of presentation

notes: Source prints decimals with a middle dot (U+00B7): 1·96, 1·31, 2·93; bound_values keep them as printed. The europepmc_core.json abstract is truncated after the primary result and does not contain the hyperglycaemia sentence; registry NCT00973154 has no results. Arm sizes n=392 (prednisone) and n=393 (placebo) are stated in the randomisation sentence ('the prednisone group (n=392) or the placebo group (n=393)'), not in the estimate span, so n_t/n_c are left null. The served row's source text uses '.' decimals, i.e. it was normalised from the record.
